contexts.text: The posterity of the Most Ancient Church, which inclined to proprium. AC 133. AC 137. AC 142. AC 190.
They did not strive after wealth.
A striving after offices merely to be seen, and to administer the goods of the lord.
They are not content with their lot, but strive after a vain kind of heavenly joy...
Affectations of elegance of speech and of learning hide the things themselves.
They... who studiously strive after reputation... for honesty.
They strive after nothing more ardently than to become gods.
Where there is no genuine marriage love it ought to be assumed, so that it may appear as if there were.
